resources.string: Import is off in Demo mode
Demo data stays in its own separate store, so an archive can never be loaded into it. Leave Demo mode in Settings to import your own archive.
Open Google Takeout in a browser and sign in with the account your Fitbit uses.
Choose only Fitbit in the list of products.
Choose ZIP as the file type. Other formats such as TGZ cannot be read.
Allow for the size. A long history can be several gigabytes, and Google may split it into more than one ZIP file.
Download the files to this phone, then pick them below. When the export comes in parts, pick all of them together.
It reads the archive on this phone. Nothing is uploaded, and the archive is never changed.
It can take a long time. It runs in the background, so you can leave this screen.
Anything already imported is skipped, so importing the same archive again is safe.
Pick one ZIP file, or every part of a split export.
This reads every file in the archive again, including ones already imported. It takes longer. Use it only if something looked wrong after an earlier import. Readings are matched, not duplicated.
Listing the files in the archive
Importing. Listing the files in the archive.
The work done so far is kept. The next import resumes where this one stopped.
Some files were damaged or cut short. What could be read was imported. Download the archive again and import it to fill the gaps.
Everything in this archive was already imported.
Rows left out (empty or low confidence)
Anything that was imported is shown next to its source in your screens.
Import is off in Demo mode. Leave Demo mode in Settings, then try again.
Your data store is not ready. Close Apex, open it again and try again.
No file was chosen. Choose the ZIP file or files from Google Takeout.
That does not look like a Takeout ZIP. Check that you picked the downloaded ZIP file, not a folder or a different file.
The ZIP is readable but holds no Fitbit data Apex can use. Request a new export from Google Takeout with Fitbit selected.
Apex could not open the file. Choose it again, and make sure it is still on this phone and the phone has free space.
This looks like a TGZ file, which Apex cannot read. Request the export again at Google Takeout and choose ZIP.
Something went wrong and the import stopped. What was already imported is kept. Try again, and the import resumes.
